title: pi-keyrouter configuration
description: Configuration for pi-keyrouter credential pools. This schema is intended for ~/.pi/keyrouter.json and provides IDE completion, hover documentation, and validation without changing keyrouter's runtime behavior.

$schema.description: Optional JSON Schema reference. Put this property first in ~/.pi/keyrouter.json to enable schema-aware completion and validation in editors that support JSON Schema. keyrouter does not add or migrate this property for existing configurations.

providers.description: Credential pools, one per provider id. Each pool contains either API keys or OAuth accounts, never both.

maxRetries.description: Maximum number of credential rotations keyrouter may make for one provider during a request. Rotation still stops as soon as a credential succeeds.

cooldownMs.description: How long, in milliseconds, a credential stays marked bad after a rate-limit or authorization failure.

overloadedCooldownMs.description: How long, in milliseconds, a provider stays marked overloaded after an overloaded response such as HTTP 529. This is provider-wide and does not count as a credential failure.

name.description: Provider id as pi knows it: a built-in id such as google or anthropic, a models.json id, or an id registered by another extension. Provider ids are matched case-insensitively.

keys.description: API keys in this pool. An empty list is allowed so the pool can be filled later with /keyrouter add. Mutually exclusive with accounts.

accounts.description: OAuth logins in this pool. An empty list is allowed so the pool can be filled later with /keyrouter add. Mutually exclusive with keys.

match.description: Legacy URL substrings. Accepted for backward compatibility but ignored; rotation is keyed by provider id instead.

takeoverOAuth.description: For a keys pool, inject pooled API keys even when pi already has a stored OAuth login for this provider. Off by default because a runtime API key shadows the stored login. Only applies to keys pools.

rotateOnQuota.description: For an accounts pool, rotate when an account-level quota or billing error is reported. Defaults to true because separate OAuth accounts are separate subscriptions. Only applies to accounts pools.

active.description: Name of the entry that was active when the last session ended. keyrouter writes and updates this field so rotation resumes across sessions; leave it out when creating a pool.

identityPath.description: Where this provider's account identity lives inside an OAuth credential. The format is level1 or level1:level2; level1 names a credential field (or dotted path), and level2 is a path into that value after automatic JWT, JSON, or base64 decoding. Examples: refresh, access:email, access:user.email, accountId:sub. Only applies to accounts pools.

sweepRefresh.description: Refresh this pool's idle OAuth accounts at session start so their tokens do not remain expired until a request needs one. Opt in per pool. Only applies to accounts pools.

apiKeyEntry.description: A named API key in a keys pool.

name.description: Human-readable name for this credential. keyrouter uses the name in status and trace output, never the key value.

value.description: The API key, either as a literal or as an environment reference in the form $NAME or ${NAME}. Environment references are expanded when the configuration loads; prefer them so secrets are not stored on disk.

accountEntry.description: A named OAuth login in an accounts pool.

name.description: Human-readable name for this account. keyrouter uses the name in status and trace output, never credential values.

accountCredential.description: An OAuth credential stored inline, in an environment variable, or in a JSON file. Inline credentials require type oauth, a non-empty access token, a refresh token, and a numeric expires timestamp in epoch milliseconds.

oneOf.description: An external credential source: @path points to a JSON file containing one credential object (a leading ~ is expanded), $NAME or ${NAME} reads a JSON credential object from an environment variable, and a string beginning with { is parsed as an inline JSON credential object.

oauthCredential.description: An OAuth credential. Provider-specific fields such as accountId, projectId, clientId, clientSecret, region, machineID, userID, and availableModelIds are preserved and are therefore allowed.

type.description: Credential type. keyrouter only pools OAuth credentials.

refresh.description: OAuth refresh token used by pi when the access token needs renewal.

expires.description: Access-token expiry as epoch milliseconds. pi refreshes the credential when fewer than about five minutes remain.

enumDescriptions: Stay on the current entry until it fails. This is the default and the historical behavior.
Advance to the next entry at every turn boundary, spreading usage across the pool.
Choose the available account whose token expires soonest. Accounts pools only; a keys pool degrades to round-robin with a warning.
Choose a uniformly random available entry at each turn boundary.
rotationStrategy.description: How the next healthy entry is selected at a turn boundary. Failure rotation still happens on top of this setting.

enumDescriptions: Show every rotation and provider-overload notification.
Hide routine rate-limit rotations and overload notices, but keep notifications that need action.
Hide rotation and overload notices. Pool exhaustion still notifies because the request has failed.
notificationLevel.description: How much keyrouter status output reaches the user. This changes notifications only; it does not change rotation behavior.
